title: Hypothesis Tests: the Normal Mean and Correlation
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Hypothesis Tests For the Mean and Correlation Worksheets
short_title: hypothesis tests for the mean and correlation
standard_text: Conduct a statistical hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution with known, given or assumed variance and interpret the results in context; use a statistical hypothesis test for correlation coefficients (the product moment correlation coefficient).
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on hypothesis testing: hypotheses for a normal mean, the distribution of the sample mean, z test statistics, critical regions, conclusions in context and tests for correlation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Compare z (or r) with the critical value and conclude in context.
body_html:
How it works

If X ~ N(μ, σ²), the mean of a sample of size n has X ~ N(μ, σ²/n). The test statistic is z = (x − μ)/(σ/√n). Reject H0 if z is in the critical region (for example z > 1.6449 for a one-tailed 5% test, |z| > 1.96 for a two-tailed 5% test).

For correlation, H0: ρ = 0. Compare the sample value r with the critical value from the table for the sample size.

Example

μ = 50, σ = 6, n = 36, x = 52. Find z.

σ/√n = 1

(52 − 50) ÷ 1

Answer: 2

Example

H1: μ > 50 at 5%. Is z = 2 significant?

2 > 1.6449

Answer: Yes: reject H0, there is evidence that the mean has increased

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by σ instead of σ/√n.
  • Using the one-tailed critical value in a two-tailed test.
  • Saying the test proves H₁, or writing hypotheses with x̄ or r instead of μ or ρ.

faq.q: What is the distribution of the sample mean?
faq.a: If X ~ N(μ, σ²), then the sample mean X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n), so its standard deviation is σ/√n.

faq.q: How do you test for correlation?
faq.a: Use H₀: ρ = 0 and H₁: ρ > 0, ρ < 0 or ρ ≠ 0. If |r| is bigger than the critical value for the sample size and significance level, reject H₀.
